The capital of Indonesia is Jakarta, on the north-west coast of Java. Since 2019 the government has been progressively moving parts of the administrative capital to Nusantara (IKN) in East Kalimantan; Jakarta remains the largest city and economic centre.

Yogyakarta (Jogja) is Java's cultural heart. Highlights: Borobudur (world's largest Buddhist temple, sunrise visits limited to timed tickets), Prambanan (Hindu temple complex, evening Ramayana ballet in dry season), Kraton (Sultan's Palace), Malioboro Street (shopping + street food), Kotagede (silver workshops), Mount Merapi jeep tours, and cheap batik courses. A 2–3 day stop is typical.

Yogyakarta is a city/regency in DIY.

Gudeg is Yogyakarta's signature dish — young jackfruit stewed for hours with coconut milk, palm sugar and spices until sweet, dark and tender. Served with rice, krecek (spicy cattle-skin stew), chicken and egg. Try it at Gudeg Yu Djum (multiple branches) or the row of night stalls on Jalan Wijilan near the Kraton. Sweet-heavy — expect a heavier palate than most other Indonesian dishes. (Source: NEX Indonesia knowledge · Special Region of Yogyakarta · verified 2026-08-30T00:00:00.000Z.)
